a: A change in one target clears the store's redo list but leaves the other targets' scenes able to redo, so the lab's Redo and a pane's own Redo disagree
SVG export writes a `{ px }` stroke's dash in user units, so the dashes on a point ring and on an untitled text box come out `scale`× longer than on screen or in a PNG
Typing a mark's title in the Marks sidebar makes one undo step per keystroke
A save in the legacy format, restored before its target has a content box, is never migrated, and its old `points` show through `get`/`query`
Every trial's Export panel uses the same radio `name`s, so two open panels take each other's selected choice
The restyle gesture counter starts again at 1 when the palette remounts, so a new restyle can merge into an older, unrelated undo step
The calibration instrument's map of picture refs gains an entry per trial and never loses one
b: The SVG export copies a `{ px }` stroke's dashes as user units, so they scale with the export where the pane and the raster export keep them in screen pixels
Restyling a selection that spans targets or trials lands one undo step per target, not one per burst
`AnnotationOverlayProps.scene` documents a shared scene separated by each mark's `target` field, but every target has its own scene
Typing a mark's title in `<MarkList>` lands one undo step per keystroke
A new mark change clears the ordering's redo for every target but leaves the other targets' scenes holding theirs, so a pane's own Redo brings back a change the store says is gone
A target the instrument no longer (or not yet) declares reads as a 0×0 content box, so its kept marks report all-zero positions and a geometry write collapses them to the origin
`calibrationInstrument` keeps a picture ref for every trial id it has ever rendered, never dropping one
Choosing "—" in `<MarkList>`'s status select stores `status: ''` rather than clearing it, so "no status" has two representations
Every API write snaps a mark's world pose to 1/10,000 of the content box, so on a large target `add` and `update` move marks by whole pixels
